s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital and adnexal inflammation
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
key_facts: Patient is an obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption and buprenorphine/naloxone use the night prior
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity is no light perception in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure is 37 mm Hg in the right eye and 21 mm Hg in the left eye
Creatinine level is 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level is 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: sudden vision loss, no light perception in one eye, and retinal findings on imaging

shortlist.label: Purtscher Retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: vision loss, retinal whitening, and history of trauma-like symptoms from heavy alcohol and medication use

shortlist.label: Posterior Scleritis
shortlist.why_kept: orbital and adnexal inflammation, elevated intraocular pressure, and retinal detachment

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: acute monocular vision loss and orbital inflammation, although less likely given patient's age

shortlist.label: Susac Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: vision loss, retinal findings, and potential systemic involvement indicated by elevated creatine kinase level

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden vision loss, severe retinal disorganization, and poor vascular perfusion, combined with a history of heavy alcohol consumption and buprenorphine/naloxone use, is consistent with Purtscher Retinopathy, which is often associated with head trauma, long bone fractures, or other forms of systemic distress, but can also be seen in the context of other systemic insults.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While it could explain the sudden vision loss, the presence of severe disorganization of the retinal architecture, subretinal fluid, and poor vascular perfusion on imaging studies suggests a more complex retinal pathology than a simple arterial occlusion.

rejected.label: Posterior Scleritis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic pain and tenderness to the globe that is typical of posterior scleritis, and the imaging findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of systemic symptoms such as headache, jaw claudication, or polymyalgia rheumatica make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Susac Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic triad of retinal vasculopathy, brain lesions, and hearing loss that is typical of Susac Syndrome.
